questions.q: What is the Scheduled Processes work area used for?
options: Only for FBDI imports and nothing else
Only for viewing financial statements
Only for installing the ADFdi Excel add-in
Submitting and tracking any long-running, asynchronous job in Oracle Fusion, including reports, batch jobs, and import processes
questions.explain: Scheduled Processes is a general-purpose work area for tracking asynchronous jobs of all kinds, not something built exclusively for FBDI.

questions.q: A product-specific import process reports status 'Succeeded.' What does that guarantee?
options: That every single row in the file was successfully imported with zero rejections
That the process will automatically re-run every night
Only that the process itself completed — individual rows inside it can still have been rejected
That the uploaded ZIP file has been deleted
questions.explain: A process-level 'Succeeded' status means the process completed. It does not by itself mean every row inside that run was accepted — rejected rows can still exist inside a succeeded process.

questions.q: What does a status of 'Error' on a scheduled process generally indicate, compared to ordinary rejected rows?
options: That the process itself failed to complete, which is typically a different and more serious problem than ordinary business-rule row rejections
The exact same thing as a row being rejected during validation
That the process succeeded perfectly
That the file was never uploaded
questions.explain: An 'Error' status means the process failed to complete at all, which is distinct from (and generally more serious than) a process that completes but rejects some rows.

questions.q: Why might a process still show as 'running' while a user wonders where the actual work is happening?
options: Because Oracle Fusion is broken
Because some processes, like Load Interface File for Import, spawn child processes that are doing the real work underneath the parent row
Because the process has already finished and the screen is just outdated
Because child processes do not exist in Oracle Fusion
questions.explain: Processes like Load Interface File for Import and Import Journals spawn child processes to do the actual work, which can be seen by expanding the parent row.

questions.q: In a busy environment with many submissions from many users, what's the best way to find your specific process run?
options: Scroll through every row on every page until you find it
There is no way to search or filter in Scheduled Processes
Ask Oracle support to find it for you every time
Filter by process name, submission date, and the user who submitted it
questions.explain: Scheduled Processes supports filtering by process name, date, and submitting user, which is the practical way to locate a specific run quickly.
